assessment.summary: Docker bridge ingress needs an explicit host-owned forwarding policy because the VPS provider offers no external firewall.

nonNegotiables: Preserve Docker bridge networking and Caddy client addresses
Do not disable Docker firewall management
assumptions: No measured packet-path performance budget was supplied
The host is dedicated to this project and unmanaged Docker state must be rejected

opportunities.title: Enforce Docker ingress inside the VPS
opportunities.summary: Add a fail-closed policy before Docker accept rules and make accidental publications loopback-only.
opportunities.diagnosis: UFW owns host INPUT while Docker-published bridge traffic follows NAT and FORWARD, leaving no independent allowlist for future container publications.

evidence.claim: The current service intentionally publishes only TCP ports 80 and 443.
The current UFW role configures host rules but no Docker forwarding hook.
A future Docker publication can bypass the UFW INPUT allowlist because Docker diverts it through NAT and FORWARD.

desiredInvariants: Only original host TCP ports 80 and 443 can reach Docker bridges from untrusted ingress.
Unqualified future Docker publications bind to loopback.
Established return traffic and container egress continue to work.
Firewall syntax and ordering are validated before public containers start.

options.title: Keep UFW-only enforcement
options.summary: Retain current host INPUT rules without Docker forwarding enforcement.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unexpected Docker publications remain externally reachable.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Publish an external sentinel port and scan it.

tradeoffs.assessment: No packet-path change.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Retain the current runtime smoke baseline.

tradeoffs.validationPlan: No additional measurement required.

tradeoffs.assessment: No deployment component changes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run existing restart smoke.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new operator contract, but exposure remains procedural.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Audit every Compose publication manually.

tradeoffs.assessment: No migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: None.

residualRisks: Any explicit Docker publication can become public.

options.title: Install third-party ufw-docker
options.summary: Use the upstream script and UFW forwarding integration.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It hooks Docker forwarding but requires a pinned privileged dependency.
Its generic policy must be narrowed and audited for this host.

tradeoffs.assessment: Docker ingress becomes UFW-controlled, with broader generic behavior than required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Audit installed after-rules and run sentinel scans.

tradeoffs.assessment: Kernel-only forwarding rules should add little overhead.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare CONNECT throughput and latency.

tradeoffs.assessment: No resident proxy is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect process and rule counts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Lifecycle depends on the external installer and reload service.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise UFW/Docker restart and reboot.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds a privileged external tool and upgrade path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Document pinning, audit and rollback.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing UFW files must be adopted by the installer.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test install/uninstall on every supported OS.

options.title: Use loopback publication behind a host TCP proxy
options.summary: Terminate public host sockets outside Docker and proxy bytes to loopback mappings.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Public traffic stays on the UFW INPUT path.
All container mappings must remain loopback-only.

tradeoffs.assessment: UFW INPUT becomes the only public ingress boundary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify no Docker mapping binds a public address.

tradeoffs.assessment: Every connection gains a userspace proxy hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure CONNECT latency and throughput.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds a proxy process and buffers.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure proxy RSS under load.

tradeoffs.assessment: The proxy becomes an additional availability dependency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise crash, restart and backpressure.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds units, logs and health checks; source IP preservation needs protocol work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Validate diagnostics and client-address behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Public listeners and health contracts move to a new component.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Stage a reversible cutover on a disposable host.

residualRisks: Proxy failure affects all public traffic
Client source identity may be lost.

acceptanceCriteria: Only host proxy sockets are public.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop proxy and restore reviewed Docker public mappings with forwarding policy in place.

options.title: Own a native DOCKER-USER policy
options.summary: Use validated Ansible-owned forwarding rules and loopback-safe Docker defaults.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Preserves intentional 80/443 while adding an independent allowlist.
Enforces policy on Docker's forwarding path.
Uses the supported hook and original-port conntrack matching.
Adds a loopback default and explicit Caddy exceptions.
Pins the iptables backend and defers nftables migration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unexpected Docker bridge ingress fails closed at a supported pre-accept hook.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run original-port sentinel scans for IPv4/IPv6.

tradeoffs.assessment: New flows perform a short chain and conntrack original-port match without a userspace hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare CONNECT latency and sustained throughput.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only bounded kernel rule state is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare rule and conntrack state under the same load.

tradeoffs.assessment: The application path is unchanged and policy is loaded before Docker, but backend ordering must survive restart/reboot.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test UFW reload, Docker restart and reboot.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators must inspect both UFW INPUT and the named Docker chain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add one verify command and recovery documentation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unmanaged Docker or firewall state must be rejected and explicitly adopted.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise clean, partial and unmanaged-host scenarios.

residualRisks: Host root or Docker daemon compromise can rewrite the policy.
Prohibited networking modes bypass the bridge hook.
A future native nftables backend requires a new policy design.
